bullets: Employment data is noisier than headlines suggest — internalizing that noise makes downstream macroeconomic decisions easier, and its second-order effects are the part most people miss.
Systems thinking in macro means watching feedback loops rather than point estimates; ignoring those loops forces a rebuild from scratch a year later.
Risk management at the central-bank level looks like reliability engineering — a pattern observed across three different teams and among teams using IEA and IPCC.
Framing determines which trade-offs are being made, so explicit framing surfaces choices that would otherwise stay hidden.
Adopting Project Drawdown within an analytical flow makes the underlying trade-off visible rather than implicit.
The trade-offs around risk management cross-cut every other theme in macroeconomics, from employment data to feedback-loop analysis.
Outside of Carbon Trust-class tooling, the failure mode is harder to spot — weaker tooling obscures where macro analysis breaks down.
Running one idea for two weeks is the recommended starting point; the rest is iteration.
